OpenEXR codec — references/image/src/codecs/openexr.rs + exr@1.74.0 Single-part scanline only (tiled/multipart/deep return Unsupported). NONE/RLE/ZIP/ZIPS/PXR24/B44/B44A/PIZ/DWAA/DWAB + half/float/uint. RLE/ZIP pipeline per OpenEXRCore internal_zip.c / internal_rle.c: separate even/odd halves, biased delta (first byte raw, rest cur-prev+128), then RLE (neg=literal -c bytes, pos=repeat c+1) / zlib-deflate. PXR24 per OpenEXRCore internal_pxr24.c: float->float24, per-row delta, MSB-first planes, zlib (reimplemented; no copied code). B44/B44A per OpenEXRCore internal_b44.c + internal_b44_table_init.c: 4x4 half blocks -> 14 bytes (3 for B44A flat fields), exact shift-search, sign-magnitude ordering, exp/log tables for pLinear. PIZ per OpenEXRCore internal_piz.c (wavelet + range bitmap) and internal_huf.c (canonical Huffman with reversed numeric order, zero-run table packing, RLE pseudo-symbol; slow-path decoder).The file layout stores each scanline channel-contiguous (ch0 row..., channels alphabetical). Our full/raw buffers are pixel-chunky. These convert at the boundary. (PXR24's own transform already produces/consumes planar rows, so it shares this boundary too.)

proc dwaDctForward(d: var array[64, float32]) {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Forward 8x8 DCT, SSE2 association + decimal constants (dctForward8x8 SSE2 path). Column-first via explicit transposes in the caller, exactly like the reference (two column passes with an in-place transpose between). Constants are the sasseembler's decimal literals, NOT cosf-computed (they differ by 1-2 ulp). 
proc dwaDctInverse(d: var array[64, float32]) {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Full 8x8 inverse DCT with the AVX association order and the sAvxCoef matrix constants (internal_dwa_simd.h IDCT_AVX_BODY), not the scalar a..g formulation. On x86-64 with AVX the reference dispatches to the AVX version, whose pairwise-sum association and differently-rounded constants change low bits vs scalar; matching it is required for bit-exact DWA decode on this platform. (On ARM the reference uses scalar/NEON paths, which round differently there too; DWA is inherently platform-specific. See dwaDctInverseScalar.) 
proc dwaDctInverseScalar(d: var array[64, float32]) {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Scalar-order 8x8 inverse DCT (dctInverse8x8_scalar, zeroedRows=0). Matches the reference on ARM/NEON and on x86 without AVX; kept for documentation and differential testing. x86-64 with AVX (this machine) uses dwaDctInverse above.

Runtime float32 division. Stops the compiler folding constant quotients (e.g. 1/2.2) in float64, which rounds 1 ulp away from the float32 result the reference computes at runtime.

proc encodeExr(img: DynamicImage; compression: int = 3): ImageResult[seq[uint8]] {.
    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Scanline writer (ZIP default; PXR24/B44/B44A/PIZ opt-in). Accepts Rgb32F/Rgba32F/Luma32F (convert first). PXR24 rounds float channels to 24 bits on write (lossy). B44 only compresses half channels, so this float-only writer stores them uncompressed (spec passthrough). HALF/UINT-exactness only matters on decode of foreign files. Channel data is packed alphabetically by name (B,G,R / A,B,G,R), per the file layout; the chlist is written in the same order.
